outcome: necessity of hospitalization in neonatal intensive therapy unit (NITU)
cohort: The study included 5066 women who gave birth in the Hospital of Siena between January 2015 and June 2019.
finding: Medically Assisted Procreation (MAP) was associated with older maternal age and less favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes compared to natural pregnancies, including higher rates of multiple pregnancy, Caesarean Section, preterm birth, lower Apgar scores, and increased neonatal intensive care admissions.
mod_finding: MAP pregnancies had a significantly higher probability of Caesarean Section (OR:4,54; 95% CI 3.28- 6.31; p < 0,001) compared to natural pregnancies.
